title: Biology 101
summary: Introductory university biology: cells, energy, genetics and evolution over 13 weeks.

audience.notes: First-year university; no prior college chemistry.

steer.focus: Build an accurate mental model of the cell and how it stores, releases and passes on information and energy.
exclude: Biochemistry detail beyond an overview of glycolysis, Krebs and electron transport

concepts.name: ATP synthesis
concepts.description: How cells make ATP from ADP using a proton gradient.
misconceptions: ATP is stored long-term in large amounts

concepts.name: Electron transport chain
concepts.description: Protein complexes that pump protons to build the gradient.
misconceptions: Oxygen is used directly to make ATP

concepts.name: Glycolysis
concepts.description: The splitting of glucose into two pyruvate with a small ATP gain.

lessons.title: Cellular respiration
lessons.summary: How cells release energy from food.

steer.focus: Trace energy from glucose to ATP, stage by stage.
include: A single running example: one glucose molecule

modules.title: Glycolysis overview
modules.summary: Splitting glucose for a small, fast energy return.

steer.focus: Inputs and outputs of glycolysis, not every step.

objectives.title: Summarise the inputs and outputs of glycolysis
objectives.statement: The learner can summarise glycolysis as glucose to two pyruvate with a net gain of two ATP and two NADH.

modules.title: The mitochondrion and ATP
modules.summary: Where most ATP is made and how.

steer.focus: The electron transport chain builds a gradient; ATP synthase spends it.
include: The analogy of a dam and a turbine

objectives.title: Explain how the mitochondrion makes ATP
objectives.statement: The learner can explain how the electron transport chain builds a proton gradient that ATP synthase uses to make ATP.

objectives.title: Compare aerobic and anaerobic ATP yield
objectives.statement: The learner can compare the ATP yield of aerobic respiration with anaerobic fermentation and say why they differ.
